READ ME FIRST — this folder is intentionally incomplete
=======================================================

Two files belong here and are NOT in this archive:

    vendor/supabase.js            @supabase/supabase-js  2.112.1
    vendor/xlsx.full.min.js       SheetJS Community Ed.  0.20.3

Until they are here, every page loads, renders, and then does nothing:
sign-in, the dashboard, and the statement of account all depend on the
Supabase client. The browser console will show 404s for the two paths
above. That is the symptom — there is no other.


WHY THEY ARE NOT INCLUDED
-------------------------
They are third-party libraries. Shipping a copy inside this archive
would mean you are trusting whoever built the archive to have fetched
the right bytes, with no way to check. sync-vendor.js fetches them from
the vendor's own CDN and records a SHA-384 of exactly what arrived, so
the check is yours rather than someone else's.


HOW TO FILL IT IN
-----------------
From the full project folder (the one holding config.js), with Node
installed and a working internet connection:

    node sync-vendor.js

It downloads both files into vendor/, verifies each against
vendor-lock.json, and refuses to write anything if a hash does not
match. Then copy the resulting vendor/ folder into the web root
alongside index.html.

If you are deploying the deploy-only archive, run the command on your
own machine against the full project archive, then upload the two
files it produces.


NO NODE? DOWNLOAD THEM BY HAND
------------------------------
Open each URL in a browser, save the file, and upload it to vendor/
under the exact filename shown. The names matter — the pages request
these two paths literally.

    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@supabase/supabase-js@2.112.1
        save as  vendor/supabase.js

    https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/package/dist/xlsx.full.min.js
        save as  vendor/xlsx.full.min.js

Note there is no path after the version on the first URL. jsDelivr
resolves a bare package URL to the package's own browser entry point.
Adding a guessed path like /dist/umd/supabase.js gives you "Couldn't
find the requested file" — that layout existed in older releases and
does not any more.

Run `node sync-vendor.js` later when convenient to generate
vendor-lock.json and confirm the bytes match.


WHY NOT JUST USE A CDN
----------------------
The pages used to load both libraries from cdn.jsdelivr.net, and the
Content-Security-Policy had to name that origin in script-src to allow
it. Naming an origin trusts EVERY script on it, not the two wanted —
a much larger hole than the one all the other CSP work closes. The
supabase tag was also @2, a floating major: whatever the CDN served at
page-load time ran with full privileges, so a bad release or a stolen
npm token reached production on the next reload with nothing in the
repo changing.

script-src is now 'self' alone. That is only true while these files are
served from this host, so please do not "fix" a 404 here by pointing a
script tag back at a CDN — it would have to be added back to the CSP in
ten places (nine pages plus .htaccess) and would undo the reason this
folder exists.


A NOTE ON THIS FILE
-------------------
.htaccess refuses to serve .txt, so this note is not reachable from the
web even though it sits in the web root.
